title: Oxygen — Passenger Service Units — Install the Secondary Retention Bracket on the Chemical Oxygen Generators
abstract: Mandatory installation of a positive secondary retention at the aft end of every chemical oxygen generator cradle, following findings of generators displaced forward with the retaining strap still fastened.

sections.planning_reason: Four chemical oxygen generators were found sitting proud of their cradles during a cabin refresh, with the retaining strap still fastened. The strap had relaxed rather than failed and the generator had walked forward under repeated pressurisation cycles. A fleet sampling of one hundred and sixty units found eleven at or beyond the displacement limit, all on aircraft above nine thousand cycles. A displaced generator still fires but the lanyard geometry is outside the qualified range, which is not acceptable for an emergency system, and the airworthiness authority issued a directive.
sections.description: This Service Bulletin gives the instructions to install a positive secondary retention at the aft end of each chemical oxygen generator cradle in the passenger service units. The retention bracket is fastened to the existing cradle through two spare holes, using new screws and a captive collar. The moulded end cap is replaced by a version with a machined recess that engages the bracket, giving a mechanical stop rather than relying on friction. The original strap is retained and re-tensioned to a defined torque. The generator, its lanyard and the mask stowage are not changed.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Make the oxygen system safe and confirm that the generators are not armed. Drop the passenger service unit on its hinge and disconnect the firing loop at the connector. Release the retaining strap and remove the generator, observing the handling precautions in AMM-T-35-20-11-200-001-A. Remove the original moulded end cap. Install the retention bracket in the two spare cradle holes using the new screws and the captive collar, and torque to the value given in the task. Fit the new end cap and confirm that the machined recess engages the bracket. Reinstall the generator and re-tension the strap to the defined torque with a calibrated wrench. Reconnect the firing loop. Do the continuity check on the firing loop. Raise the service unit and latch it. Repeat for every service unit. Record the modification and update the cabin configuration record.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to the listed TTN-88W1 and TTN-88W2 aircraft only. These are the aircraft above the cycle threshold at which displacement was found, and the fleet sampling confirmed that no aircraft below the threshold is affected. Aircraft on the later cradle standard are outside the effectivity.
sections.material_note: Kit K3520-1006-01 covers one full cabin and is sized to the highest density layout; unused parts may be returned. The end cap is a fourteen week lead item. Removed end caps are scrapped locally.

type_data.compliance_time: Within 18 months after the effective date of the associated airworthiness directive.
